explanations: luna: Adam and his spouse are expelled from the Garden, the inverse of the section's last invitation to enter God's Garden. | terra: Satan causes the pair to slip and brings them out of the Garden; this forced خروج is the narrative reverse of the closing invitation to enter God's Garden.

luna: Moses is promised forty nights before the people turn to the calf; this is another counted span of successive nights beside the section's plural ten nights. | terra: The appointment of forty nights is another explicit counting of successive darknesses, though it lacks 7:142’s separate ten-night completion.

luna: When Moses strikes the rock, water bursts from it in انفَجَرَتْ; the same root's force of opening out adds a concrete outflow to the section's dawn-splitting image. | terra: Water bursts from struck rock as twelve springs; the section’s f-j-r root here names a physical rupture through a hard cover rather than dawn through darkness.
terra: Rocks from which rivers burst show the same f-j-r mechanism in matter: what was enclosed breaks outward through stone.
terra: The alternation of night and day appears among signs for people who reason; the broader catalogue still concretely echoes the oath’s appeal to a discerning mind.

luna: The white thread separates from the black at مِنَ الْفَجْرِ: dawn appears first as a fine boundary, just as the section describes. | terra: The white thread becoming distinct from the black thread مِنَ ٱلْفَجْرِ makes dawn the fine separating line described in the section, not a fully lit expanse.
luna: The verse calls God's ordinances boundaries and forbids crossing them; it states in law the containing function that the section gives the mind's inner wall.
luna: Abraham asks for a sign of revival so that his heart may be reassured; in the section's resurrection-to-return arc, this gives reassurance a concrete relation to seeing what follows death.
terra: Those seeking forgiveness in the pre-dawn hours inhabit the last thin portion of the night just before the section’s opening rent.

luna: Night enters into day and day into night; the verse gives another direct formulation of the two states passing through one another. | terra: God makes night enter day and day enter night, then brings living from dead; the section’s two moving edges and its grave-to-life transition appear together.
terra: Every نفس tastes death, and success is being removed from the Fire and admitted to the Garden; one ayah traces the section’s passage from death-cover to garden entry.
terra: The alternation of night and day is a sign for أُو۟لِى ٱلْأَلْبَٰبِ, closely matching an oath from night and dawn addressed to the possessor of حِجْر.
luna: The verse warns that crossing God's limits leads to the Fire; it states the consequence of failing the containing boundary that the section gives to ḥijr.
terra: Believers are admitted to gardens and into deep, abundant shade; the ayah explicitly combines garden-entry with the sheltering cover developed in the section.
terra: No one but God can remove affliction; this is a direct Qur'anic counterpart to the source section's secondary dictionary example of anxiety lifting away.
terra: In distress people call on God and He removes what prompted the call if He wills, enacting the section's secondary sense of a burden being uncovered.
terra: God takes people during the night and raises them again by day; the nightly cover becomes a small death whose removal restores wakeful life.
terra: God shows Abraham the dominion of heavens and earth so that he may have certainty; it states the purpose of the night-sky discernment enacted in 6:76–79.

luna: The root of the section's root ج ن ن appears in the night that covers Abraham; seeing the star and then its setting makes darkness a ground for discernment, not mere concealment. | terra: جَنَّ عَلَيْهِ ٱلَّيْلُ uses the section’s own covering root: night covers Abraham yet lets the star appear, making darkness a setting for discerning what sets from what does not.

luna: Abraham next sees the moon and watches it set; 6:76 begins the same night-covered sequence with a star, and this verse makes setting a repeated test of what can be divine. | terra: The setting moon repeats the test first made with the star, showing that the night-cover permits a sequence of comparisons rather than one isolated sight.

luna: The sun, larger than the moon, also sets, completing the sequence begun in 6:76; 6:79 then states Abraham's turn to the Creator of heaven and earth. | terra: The rising and then setting sun carries Abraham’s test across the dawn boundary into daylight, and its setting prevents daylight’s greater brightness from being confused with permanence.

luna: Abraham turns to the Creator after the star, moon, and sun have set; this completes 6:76-78's use of night to distinguish the setting from what remains. | terra: Abraham turns toward the Creator of heavens and earth after the setting lights; this supplies the non-setting referent toward which the covered-night observations lead.
terra: God splits the grain and date-stone before 6:96 calls Him the splitter of daybreak; hidden life and hidden morning emerge by the same فلق action.

luna: The section's root ف ج ر names dawn's splitting; here God is فَالِقُ الْإِصْبَاحِ, the one who cleaves morning from night. | terra: فَالِقُ ٱلْإِصْبَاحِ names God as the splitter of daybreak; it gives an agent to the section’s image of darkness cracking open at dawn.
terra: The stars guide through the darknesses of land and sea; like Abraham's star, a light within darkness makes orientation possible instead of merely being obscured by the cover.
terra: حِجْر here is a humanly invented ban on crops and cattle; this secondary use is a caution that an external prohibition can masquerade as the sound inward restraint praised in the section.
luna: Satan tempts the pair so that what was concealed of their nakedness becomes apparent; this contrasts exposure caused by disobedience with dawn's clear opening.
luna: After eating, the pair's nakedness appears and they cover themselves with Garden leaves; wrongdoing brings a shameful exposure, unlike dawn's revealing light.
terra: Clothing covers nakedness while “the garment of taqwā” is better; it gives Qur’anic form to the section’s dictionary metaphor of a religious cover that فجور tears.

luna: Satan's expulsion of Adam's parents from the Garden includes stripping their clothes; it reverses the section's final entry and makes concealment fail through disobedience. | terra: Satan expels Adam's parents from the Garden while stripping their clothing to expose them; garden-exit and lost cover become one moral reversal of the section's final entry into shelter.

luna: The proud are barred from the Garden, with a gate that will not open and entry made impossible; this joins the section's wall-like restraint to its final Garden threshold. | terra: The deniers cannot enter the Garden until a camel passes through a needle’s eye; garden entry here is barred, illuminating the unimpeded command at the surah’s end.
terra: A veil separates the people of the Garden and Fire while those on the heights recognize both groups, joining eschatological boundary, discernment, and the hoped-for Garden.
terra: “Enter the Garden; no fear upon you, nor shall you grieve” closely parallels the reassured addressee summoned into the final garden.

luna: Night and day are made to cover and pursue one another swiftly, presenting the same layered, moving boundary that the section gives to the night and dawn. | terra: يُغْشِى ٱلَّيْلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ describes night as a cover laid over day, while يَطْلُبُهُ حَثِيثًا makes that cover move rather than remain fixed.
terra: Rain brings varied fruits from dead land and becomes an analogy for bringing out the dead, joining growing cover above the earth with release from beneath it.

luna: Moses' appointed time is counted as thirty nights completed by ten; this gives the section's ten nights a Quranic counterpart as successive nights rather than one dark span. | terra: Moses’ appointment is thirty nights completed by ten; the explicit addition of عَشْر makes this the clearest external counterpart to the section’s counted ten nights.

luna: The mountain is made level in دَكًّا at the theophany; the same root as the section's crushed earth appears in a scene of divine force breaking a solid surface. | terra: When divine manifestation makes the mountain دَكًّا, the same root as 89:21 joins crushing ground to a theophanic scene, closely anticipating the crushed earth before the Lord’s coming in 89:21–22.
terra: The moon's measured phases disclose the number of years and calculation; it connects visible nocturnal light with the section's counting of successive nights.
terra: The alternation of night and day and what God created within them are signs for the mindful, another explicit audience for the same cosmic transition.

luna: The faces of those who earned evil are covered with pieces of dark night; this makes darkness a judgment-cover, a moral counter-image to dawn's opening light. | terra: Faces covered with pieces of dark night turn the section's sheltering natural cover into an image of humiliation and punishment.

luna: Night is made for rest and day for sight; the verse gives a concrete human consequence of the section's covered darkness and opened visibility. | terra: Night is made for rest and day for sight; the functional contrast clarifies darkness as shelter without treating it as mere blindness.
terra: If harm touches a person none but God can remove it, a repeated formulation of the section's nonvisual “worry lifted” branch.

luna: Lot is told to travel by night with his family using the same س ر ي root as the section's moving night; here people move under night rather than night itself moving. | terra: The command to travel by a portion of the night uses the same س ر ي sense as 89:4, and “their appointment is the morning” makes dawn the journey’s decisive limit.
terra: The two edges of day and near portions of night divide worship across the same moving light-dark boundaries the section stages.
terra: The نفس that commands evil is the moral opposite of the tranquil soul; it shows why an inward restraint is needed before the final invitation.
terra: The histories of earlier peoples contain a lesson for people of understanding, directly explaining how Surah 89's destruction narratives answer its question to the possessor of حِجْر.
terra: God covers day with night, then calls these signs for people who reflect; this repeats both the moving cover and the discerning audience of the section's oath.
terra: The one hiding by night is set against the one moving openly by day, giving the natural cover a concrete human use and daylight its disclosure.

luna: The righteous enter Eden with their families, and angels greet them at its gates; this develops the section's entry among God's servants and into the Garden. | terra: The righteous enter Gardens of Eden together with righteous kin, expanding the final invitation “among My servants” into a gathered community.
terra: Angels enter upon them through every gate with a greeting of peace, making the garden boundary permeable to welcome rather than exclusion.
luna: The hearts become tranquil, تَطْمَئِنُّ الْقُلُوبُ, echoing the section's نَفْسُ الْمُطْمَئِنَّةُ and giving a distinct Quranic setting for inward rest.
terra: The promised Garden has lasting fruit and lasting shade; its enduring shade makes concrete the section’s derivation of janna from trees covering the ground.
terra: The God-conscious are amid gardens and springs immediately before the command to enter safely, presenting the garden as an encompassing place of shelter.
terra: “Enter them in peace, secure” is a direct garden-entry command whose safety clarifies the sheltering quality of the section’s final cover.
terra: No weariness touches the Garden's people and they will never be made to leave it; permanent non-exit sharpens the section's dictionary contrast between دخول and خروج.

luna: Lot is again told to travel during part of the night with س ر ي; the repeated command gives the section's night-journey root a concrete human scene. | terra: Travel with the family during a portion of night repeats the same س ر ي night-journey and makes movement through darkness the means of escape.
terra: The decree that the people will be cut off by morning makes dawn the fixed terminus of the family’s night journey in 15:65.
terra: The blast seizes the people at sunrise, disclosing the destructive outcome that lay beyond the commanded night departure.

luna: The name al-Hijr echoes the section's ḥijr, but this verse uses it as a place-name; its people deny messengers, while 15:82-83 supply the rock-carving and morning-destruction scene that links them to the surah's Thamud.
luna: The people called Companions of al-Hijr carve homes into mountains and feel secure; this recalls 89:9's Thamud cutting rock, and 15:83 completes their fate at morning.

luna: The same stone-carving people are seized by a cry at morning; this turns dawn into the hour of punishment, a counter-scene to the section's light breaking the night, while 15:82 supplies their carved homes.
terra: Night, day, sun, moon, and stars are subjected as signs for people who reason; the cosmic scene explicitly calls for the faculty the section names حِجْر.
terra: The righteous enter Gardens of Eden with flowing rivers and fulfilled desires; it supplies the concealed reward into which 16:32’s death-time greeting admits them.

luna: At death the angels greet the good and tell them to enter the Garden; this closely joins the section's calm soul, peaceful return, and final command to enter. | terra: The angels take the good in death saying “Peace” and “Enter the Garden,” explicitly joining the soul’s death-transition, peace, and entry.
terra: When God removes harm, the affliction passes like a lifted cover, though the ayah warns that some then associate partners with Him.

luna: The verse describes a heart secure in faith even when the person is compelled to speak otherwise; this gives the section's tranquil soul a specific inward counterpart amid its contrast between moral rupture and faithful restraint.

luna: The night journey begins with أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِ لَيْلًا; the same root depicts a human journey through night, alongside the section's night moving on. | terra: أَسْرَىٰ بِعَبْدِهِۦ لَيْلًا states the section’s dictionary sense of surā exactly: a divinely conducted journey during the night.

luna: The night sign is made dark and the day sign gives sight; this states the concealment and disclosure that the section makes into a slit of dawn. | terra: The erased sign of night and the sight-giving sign of day connect darkness and visibility, while the reckoning of years links the succession of nights to counted time.
terra: Invoked beings cannot remove or transfer harm, setting a boundary around who can perform the release illustrated by the section's lifted-anxiety example.

luna: The dawn recitation is singled out as witnessed, locating الفجر at the transition from night into a distinct morning interval, as in the section's threshold image. | terra: Prayer is marked from the sun’s decline through night’s darkness to قُرْءَانَ ٱلْفَجْرِ; dawn again serves as a witnessed liturgical boundary.
terra: The demand that a spring be made to gush from the earth uses the section’s f-j-r root for an opening through ground rather than night.
luna: The requested garden of palms and vines includes streams bursting through it in تُفَجِّرَ; the root joins an opening flow to the garden that closes the section.
luna: The garden is framed by vines and palms surrounding it, حَفَفْنَاهُمَا بِنَخْلٍ; this gives a Quranic scene for the section's garden as foliage that hides the earth.

luna: Between the two gardens a stream is made to burst in فَجَّرْنَا, uniting the section's root for dawn's rupture with its final covered garden. | terra: God makes a river gush between two gardens; the physical f-j-r branch and the garden-cover meet in a single cultivated scene.

luna: The barrier is made level in دَكَّاءَ when God's promise arrives; this joins the section's pounding root to a boundary finally flattened. | terra: The protective barrier becomes دَكَّآء when God’s promise comes true; this ayah brings the section’s wall and its crushing verb into one scene of a boundary levelled at the appointed time.
terra: Eyes that were under a covering from remembrance could not see; unlike Abraham’s night-cover, this inward cover prevents the very discernment darkness enabled for him.
terra: The promised Gardens of Eden belong to the unseen, directly supporting the section's claim that the garden reward is presently hidden yet certain to arrive.
terra: Humans are created from earth, returned into it, and brought out again; the whole sequence distinguishes temporary soil-cover from final emergence.

luna: Moses is commanded to travel at night with his people using the same root; the passage makes night a route crossed by travelers, alongside the section's personified night journey. | terra: The command to take the servants by night uses the section’s س ر ي sense and leads directly to a dry path opened through the sea, joining night travel to an opening.
terra: God will blast the mountains away, initiating an explicit removal of the earth's raised features before the level plain of 20:106–107.
terra: The removed mountains leave a level, bare plain, a direct scene-parallel to the ground made flat by dakk.
terra: No crookedness or elevation remains visible in the plain, stating the completed levelling contributed by the preceding mountain-removal.
luna: The destroyed generations' abandoned homes are a lesson for people of understanding; this connects the section's reason-as-restraint with the warning carried by the ruined peoples in surah 89.
terra: Glorification before sunrise and sunset, during portions of night, and at the day's ends marks the same perceptible thresholds the section's oaths stage.
terra: The heavens and earth were joined and then split apart, a cosmic nonlexical parallel to a concealed expanse opened by a decisive cleft.
terra: Night, day, sun, and moon each travel in an orbit, giving cosmic motion to the same succession that the section pictures as a travelling night.
terra: Every soul tastes death, is tested, and returns to God; it preserves the section's sequence from نفس through death-cover to return, though it does not itself name the Garden.
terra: God removes Job’s affliction; it is a concrete Qur’anic counterpart to the section’s secondary dictionary example of worry being lifted away as a cover clears.
terra: God will raise those in the graves, stating the promised reversal of the earth-cover whose physical opening other Last-Day ayat depict.

luna: The verse again says that night enters day and day enters night, placing the section's slit of dawn within a recurring transition. | terra: God makes night enter day and day enter night; the reciprocal دخول renders their boundary as continual passage rather than a fixed line.

luna: At death a person pleads, رَبِّ ارْجِعُونِ, to be sent back; this reverses the section's serene soul being told to return to its Lord. | terra: At death the wrongdoer asks to be sent back; this desperate, refused return contrasts with the peaceful soul’s welcomed return to its Lord, completed by the barrier in 23:100.

luna: A barrier stands before the dead until resurrection, بَرْزَخٌ; 23:99 supplies the plea to return, contrasting that blocked passage with the section's welcomed return to God. | terra: A barzakh stands behind the dead until resurrection, making the grave an uncrossable interim boundary rather than the open garden-entry offered to the tranquil soul.
terra: Layered darkness in the deep sea leaves a person barely able to see even a raised hand; this marks the limit where darkness ceases to aid discrimination and overwhelms sight.
terra: God’s turning of night and day contains a lesson for people of sight, joining the moving cover to the perceiver whom the oath expects to discern it.

luna: The verse names the time before the dawn prayer as a household privacy period; it treats الفجر as a precise boundary in daily life, like the section's narrow dawn line. | terra: “Before the dawn prayer” and “after the night prayer” define two privacy thresholds, showing how dawn and night boundaries order embodied daily life.

luna: The criminals call حِجْرًا مَحْجُورًا when they see the angels; the exact root named for reason-as-restraint appears here as an impassable boundary at judgment. | terra: حِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا is the section’s own outward, eschatological form of حِجْر: a boundary declared when the angels become visible and good news is barred from the guilty.

luna: Night again is made a garment, while sleep is rest and day is renewed activity; it develops the section's cover-and-opening scene as a human rhythm. | terra: God makes night a garment, sleep a repose, and day a rising; this one sequence joins cover, death-like concealment, and renewed emergence.
terra: حِجْرًا مَّحْجُورًا names the restraining boundary between two meeting bodies of water, giving the section’s inner wall a concrete cosmic analogue.

luna: Moses receives the same night-travel command from the س ر ي root, extending the section's moving-night word into the Exodus scene. | terra: “Travel by night with My servants” repeats the same root and speaker-pattern as the section’s moving night, here as a saving departure before morning pursuit.
terra: The sea splits after Moses strikes it, supplying the opened path that answers the commanded night journey in 26:52.
terra: The barrier placed between two seas repeats the section's outward model for حِجْر: a boundary that prevents two moving domains from overrunning one another.
terra: God answers the distressed and removes evil, preserving the section’s secondary “anxiety lifted” sense as an experienced release rather than a visual dawn.
terra: God guides people through the darknesses of land and sea, another specific instance in which darkness contains the means of finding a way rather than abolishing perception.
terra: Night provides repose while day gives sight, repeating the complementary uses of cover and disclosure for people who can perceive the sign.

luna: The counterfactual asks who could bring light if God made night perpetual; it reverses the section's dawn breaking the night-cover by imagining the break withheld. | terra: The question about a perpetual night asks who could bring light, exposing what dawn’s opening gives by imagining the cover never lifted.

luna: The companion question asks who could bring night if God made day perpetual; it marks the other boundary of the cycle whose night-to-dawn edge opens the section. | terra: The question about perpetual day asks who could bring a night for rest, preventing the section’s dawn from making darkness merely negative.
terra: Night for rest and day for seeking bounty are paired mercies; their distinct gifts explain why the boundary between cover and disclosure must keep moving.
terra: Every soul tastes death and then returns to God, reproducing the closing soul's death-threshold and return before 29:58 supplies its Garden lodging.
terra: Believers are lodged in lofty chambers of the Garden after the soul's death and return in 29:57, completing the same movement from mortality into shelter.
terra: The command to glorify God at evening and morning explicitly places worship at the passage into and out of night.
terra: Praise at late day and noon completes 30:17's morning-evening frame, spreading remembrance across the cycle's visible stages.
terra: At one divine call people come out of the earth; this closely reverses grave-cover and parallels the soul being summoned toward its Lord.

luna: Night and day enter one another while sun and moon run to term; this develops the section's moving night as part of a measured cycle. | terra: The mutual entry of night and day shows each cover sliding into the other, a direct analogue for night going and leaving what it covered exposed.

luna: The promised comfort is something hidden from people today, أُخْفِيَ لَهُم; this states directly the concealed reward that the section hears inside جَنَّتِي. | terra: No soul knows what delight has been hidden for them; this explicitly states the section’s account of Paradise as a reward still covered from present sight.
terra: Gardens of refuge (جَنَّاتُ ٱلْمَأْوَىٰ) are the believers’ lodging, explicitly presenting Paradise as the sheltering cover developed in the section.
terra: The people are told to travel safely through the linked settlements by nights and days, a nonlexical parallel to night as a traversed interval.

luna: The same night-into-day and day-into-night motion is repeated alongside the sun and moon's appointed course, another specific formulation of the section's boundary crossing. | terra: The entry of night into day and day into night stages the section’s opening and closing movements as two directions of one governed transition.
terra: Barriers before and behind plus a covering over sight leave people unable to see; it is an imposed wall that blinds, opposite the inward حِجْر that enables right judgment.
terra: The slain believer is told “Enter the Garden,” a compact instance of the section’s movement from death to the covered reward.

luna: The night is a sign when God strips the day from it in نَسْلَخُ; this reverses the section's dawn splitting into night, while preserving the image of light withdrawn from darkness. | terra: God strips day from night and people are left in darkness; this reverses the section’s dawn-image, where darkness is the layer removed and light appears beneath it.
terra: Day cannot overtake night and each travels in an orbit; this supplies the firm boundary within which the section’s cover and dawn-opening succeed one another.

luna: People hurry from the graves toward their Lord, مِنَ الْأَجْدَاثِ إِلَىٰ رَبِّهِمْ; the grave's cover gives way to the soul's final approach to the Lord. | terra: Those in the graves rush from them toward their Lord, directly continuing the section’s contrast between the earth-cover and the soul’s call toward God.
luna: Those raised from their resting place ask who awakened them; 36:51 supplies the graves they have just left, completing the section's movement from grave-cover toward the Lord.
terra: The people of the Garden and their spouses recline in shade, making the final cover a place of rest and companionship.
terra: People pass the ruins of the destroyed community in the morning; daylight exposes the remnant of transgression, much as the section’s dawn precedes its ruined peoples.
terra: They also pass the ruins at night and are asked whether they will reason, joining night, destroyed transgressors, and the section’s appeal to inward understanding.
terra: When punishment descends into a people's courtyard, it is called an evil morning for those warned; dawn here discloses judgment rather than relief.
terra: The ayah refuses to equate corrupters with believers or the God-conscious with ٱلْفُجَّارِ; it joins 89:11–12’s فساد to the section’s فجر/فجور opposition.

luna: The verse portrays night and day coiling over one another, a repeated wrapping and unwrapping that enlarges the section's single opening into a cycle. | terra: God “wraps” night over day and day over night; the reciprocal wrapping supplies the section’s sliding-cover mechanism in both directions.
terra: Those who listen and follow the best word are the people of understanding; the ayah describes how the inward faculty called حِجْر actually restrains choice.
terra: False objects of worship cannot remove harm God intends, again distinguishing the true agent who can lift what weighs upon a person.
terra: God takes the الأنفس at death and during sleep, retains one and releases another; this directly binds the closing نفس to concealment, return, and the death threshold.

luna: Those rejecting their Lord are told to enter Hell's gates; 39:73 follows with the Garden's gates opening, framing the section's final invitation as the blessed side of a divided destination. | terra: The arrogant are commanded to enter Hell's gates immediately before the righteous enter the Garden in 39:73; the same threshold-action leads to opposite enclosures.

luna: The Garden's gates open and its keepers welcome those entering; the verse supplies the threshold and welcome implicit in the section's repeated command to enter. | terra: The righteous are told at the Garden’s gates to enter and remain; the threshold makes the section’s final دخول a visible crossing into enclosure.
terra: God makes night for rest and day sight-giving; the recurrent pair supports the section’s distinction between a useful cover and its illuminating removal.
terra: Angels descend on the steadfast at death with “do not fear or grieve” and glad tidings of the promised Garden, closely echoing the reassurance around the final soul-call.
terra: Within the promised reward, people receive whatever their souls desire; the closing نفس and its still-hidden delight meet in the continuation of 41:30's death-time reassurance.
terra: The promised delights are a welcoming provision from the Forgiving, Merciful, characterizing the hidden Garden as hospitality after the angels' reassurance.
terra: Night, day, sun, and moon are signs, but people must worship their Creator rather than the luminaries; this states the theological discrimination enacted by Abraham under night-cover.
terra: “Yā ʿibādī” addresses God’s servants with freedom from fear and grief, the closest external summons to the peaceful soul invited among “My servants” at the surah’s end.
terra: This ayah identifies the addressed servants as those who believed and submitted, specifying who receives the no-fear summons of 43:68 and entry command of 43:70.
terra: “Enter the Garden” addresses those servants directly, reproducing the section’s final movement from divine call to entry into the garden-cover.
terra: After the command to enter the Garden, it contains what souls desire and eyes delight in, unfolding the concealed joy promised to the final soul.

luna: The command to travel by night repeats the section's س ر ي root; its context makes night the passage through which a people depart. | terra: The command to journey by night with God’s servants gives the same س ر ي action and makes the darkness a passage toward deliverance.
terra: Leaving the sea رهوا after the night journey supplies an opened passage that remains behind once the travellers have gone through, completing 44:23’s scene.
terra: The alternation of night and day is called a sign for people who reason, directly pairing the section’s temporal scene with its “possessor of restraint.”
terra: Every soul arrives with a driver and witness immediately before its covering is removed in 50:22, identifying whose final perception is uncovered.
terra: “We removed from you your covering” (فَكَشَفْنَا عَنكَ غِطَآءَكَ) makes sight sharp on the Last Day, extending the section’s removal of a cover from physical dawn to final perception.
terra: The near Garden is promised to every returning, guarding person; “returning” and “guarding” join the final return to God with the section’s inward restraint.
terra: Coming with a penitent heart while fearing the Merciful unseen explains the inner disposition immediately before “Enter it in peace” in 50:34.

luna: The invitation is explicit: enter it in peace; the destination and secure entry echo the section's final call to enter the Garden. | terra: ٱدْخُلُوهَا بِسَلَٰمٍ commands entry into the near Garden in peace, closely matching the tranquil soul’s final invitation to enter.
terra: The command to glorify before sunrise and before sunset turns the two light-boundaries into moments of addressed attention.
terra: Glorification during the night continues the boundary-command of 50:39 through the covering interval itself.
terra: The earth splits open from the dead as they hasten out, reversing burial-cover through an opening strikingly like dawn’s rent in darkness.
terra: Seeking forgiveness at the pre-dawn hours gives the retreating end of night a specific devotional action before light appears.
terra: Glorification at night and at the retreat of the stars marks the observable moment when the night-cover and its lights withdraw together.
terra: The lote tree stands at the furthest boundary, bringing an actual tree and a terminal limit together immediately beside the Garden of Refuge.
terra: The Garden of Refuge lies beside the boundary-tree, making Paradise explicitly an enclosing shelter at a limit.
terra: The lote tree is covered by what covers it, an unusually direct meeting of tree, covering action, and the adjacent Garden whose name the section derives from cover.
terra: The moon itself is split as the Hour approaches; instead of darkness cracking to disclose a light, a visible night-light becomes the object of rupture.
terra: People emerge from the graves with lowered eyes like scattered locusts, giving movement and visibility to what had been hidden under burial.

luna: The earth's springs burst forth in فَجَّرْنَا after the flood, carrying the section's root ف ج ر from dawn's opening into water breaking out of the ground. | terra: The earth is burst into springs until waters meet for a decreed event, enlarging the root-image from a slit of light to openings across the ground.
terra: Lot’s family is saved at the last pre-dawn hour, making the receding edge of night the boundary between refuge and judgment.
terra: A lasting punishment overtakes the people in the morning, the judgment-side of the dawn boundary whose saving side appears in 54:34.
luna: The command not to transgress the balance gives a specific moral limit, echoing the restraint that the section hears in ḥijr.
terra: The two seas are released to meet, establishing the moving bodies whose non-transgression is explained by the barrier in 55:20.
terra: Between the meeting seas is a barrier they do not transgress; this is a concrete outward model of restraint holding movement within its proper limit.

luna: One of the descriptions of Paradise is two gardens with branches; the garden word and boughs give a concrete leafy cover for the section's hidden, tree-covered jannah. | terra: The two gardens are described as possessing spreading branches, supporting the section’s lexical picture of a garden whose trees cover what lies beneath.
luna: The gardens are dark green and dense; this gives another Quranic picture of the foliage that the section hears in the root ج ن ن.
terra: The earth is convulsed violently, beginning a three-ayah dissolution of ground and mountains that closely parallels the dakk scene.
terra: The mountains are pulverized completely, supplying the crushing action that follows the earth's convulsion in 56:4.
terra: The pulverized mountains become scattered dust, showing the exposed residue after the stable earthly cover has been broken down.

luna: The garden scene begins with thornless lote trees; 56:29-30 continue with clustered branches and extended shade, supplying the leafy shelter behind the section's final Garden image. | terra: The reward contains thornless lote trees, supplying one part of the actual tree-canopy behind the extended shade named in 56:30.

luna: The next detail is clustered talh trees; 56:28 begins the same garden vegetation and 56:30 names its extended shade. | terra: Layered acacia or banana trees add the second concrete canopy immediately before the passage names extended shade.

luna: Extended shade covers the people of the right; 56:28-29 identify the trees, making this verse's shelter a concrete parallel to the section's covered Garden. | terra: Extended shade in the reward scene isolates the sheltering function that the section hears within the word janna.

luna: Night and day enter into one another here, a specific formulation of the threshold crossing that the section stages as a cover shifting away. | terra: God makes night enter day and day enter night; its language of entry also echoes the final command to enter the garden after the night-image has passed.
terra: The wall with a gate has mercy inside and punishment outside; it makes an eschatological boundary sort people just as the section’s حِجْر restrains and distinguishes.
luna: Hypocrites take their oaths as a shield, جُنَّةً, using the same covering root named for night and Garden; here concealment protects falsehood rather than opening into light.

terra: After a people's strongholds fail and their dwellings are ruined, the audience is told to take warning, O people of sight; this matches Surah 89's destroyed peoples addressed to one capable of discernment.
luna: Their oaths are again a shield, جُنَّةً, but now explicitly conceal their rejection; it gives the section's cover-root a morally opposite use.
luna: Success is tied to being protected from the self's avarice; this is a concrete inward restraint comparable to the section's reason-as-barrier.

luna: The condemned say that listening or reasoning would have kept them from the Fire; this makes the section's “reason as inner wall” concrete as restraint that could have prevented transgression. | terra: The people of the Fire say that listening or reasoning would have restrained them from their end; this is the failed moral function the section’s dictionary gives to حِجْر.
terra: The owners swear to harvest their garden in the morning; a garden and an anticipated dawn are deliberately placed in one test-scene.
terra: A visitation circles the garden while its owners sleep, so the night-cover conceals a decisive change from human sight.
terra: By morning the garden has become like a dark, stripped field; dawn reveals loss where the section’s final Garden promises shelter.
terra: The owners call one another at morning, moving from the hidden event of 68:19 to human recognition after light returns.

luna: The earth and mountains are pounded in فَدُكَّتَا دَكَّةً وَاحِدَةً, a direct parallel to 89:21's repeated pounding of the earth. | terra: The earth and mountains are lifted and crushed with one دَكَّة, the clearest repeated Last-Day use of the section’s d-k-k image.
terra: The sky splits and becomes frail on the day when earth and mountains have been crushed, continuing the dakk scene from ground to celestial cover.
terra: They rush from the graves as though toward a marker, another explicit transition from enclosed earth to exposed assembly.
terra: Human growth from the earth like vegetation links the opened ground to life and anticipates return beneath that same surface.
terra: God returns people into the earth and brings them out again, making burial-cover a passage rather than their lasting enclosure.
terra: The shaking earth and mountains reduced to a loose heap of sand form a close physical parallel to the earth's repeated pounding in 89:21.
terra: God measures the varying portions of night and day while worshippers stand through them, linking successive nights to exact temporal measure.

luna: Night turns its back in أَدْبَرَ; the next oath names the clearing morning, matching the section's moving cover and its opening. | terra: The night “when it turns its back” gives the section’s travelling night a visible departure immediately before the whitening morning of 74:34.

luna: Morning brightens in أَسْفَرَ, completing 74:33's departing night and giving a second formulation of the section's dawn. | terra: The morning “when it brightens” supplies the revealed side of the section’s two-part motion: night withdraws and what lay beneath becomes visible.
terra: Every soul is held in pledge for what it earned shortly after the oaths by departing night and brightening morning, linking the dawn scene to moral accountability.
terra: The self-reproaching نفس stands between moral rupture and tranquillity, providing a distinct self-state against which the section’s final addressee can be heard.

luna: The person wants to keep sinning ahead, لِيَفْجُرَ أَمَامَهُ; the root's moral branch makes a deliberate breach where dawn's rupture brings light. | terra: The human wants to continue in فُجُور ahead of him; this is the section’s moral f-j-r branch as an ongoing breach of limits rather than a release of light.
terra: God’s servants drink from a spring they make gush forth (يُفَجِّرُونَهَا تَفْجِيرًا); the f-j-r burst and “servants” meet on the garden side of the section’s closing image.
terra: God rewards patience with a Garden and silk, identifying the garden scene whose close shade is described in 76:14 as recompense.
terra: Those reclining in the Garden see neither burning sun nor bitter cold, specifying what the close shade of 76:14 shelters them from.

luna: In the Garden, shade lies close over its people and its fruits hang low; this gives a concrete leafy shelter for the section's hidden, tree-covered Garden image. | terra: In the garden reward, its shade is drawn close over them; the garden’s cover is experienced as shelter rather than the darkness or soil-cover left behind.
terra: The God-conscious are amid shades and springs; protective cover and released water meet as favorable counterparts to the section’s garden and bursting images.
terra: Sleep is made for repose immediately before night is called a garment, adding the death-like stillness that the section later sets beside burial.

luna: The night is called a garment, لِبَاسًا, directly naming the covering that the section's dawn tears open. | terra: “We made the night a garment” gives literal Qur’anic form to the section’s night spread over things as a covering.
terra: Day is made for livelihood immediately after night’s garment, giving the uncovered interval its active human purpose.
luna: This verse says God darkened the night and brought out its morning brightness, staging the cover and its opening as two successive acts.

luna: The one who restrains the self from desire, نَهَى النَّفْسَ عَنِ الْهَوَىٰ, embodies the inner wall that the section says reason places against wrongdoing. | terra: The one who fears standing before the Lord and restrains the نفس from desire enacts the inner wall that the section says prevents unfitting action.

luna: That person's refuge is the Garden; 79:40 supplies the restraint that leads to a destination echoing the section's final Garden-entry. | terra: For the self restrained in 79:40, Paradise is the refuge; the pair joins the section’s inward حِجْر to the final garden shelter.

luna: God causes the human to die and be placed in a grave, فَأَقْبَرَهُ; this makes the section's grave-as-cover sense concrete at the passage from life to burial. | terra: God causes the human being to die and be buried; this is the explicit Qur’anic scene corresponding to the section’s secondary “grave-cover” sense.
terra: The earth is split open so growth can emerge; like dawn, an enclosing surface parts and what was hidden beneath becomes manifest.
terra: Dense, luxuriant gardens emerge in the sequence begun by the earth's splitting in 80:26, joining a rent in the ground to the tree-cover it produces.
luna: The wicked at judgment are called al-fajarah; the dawn-root's moral branch describes a human outcome opposite to the light opening in the section.
terra: Every soul knows what it has brought before the oaths by the retreating night and breathing morning, so the cosmic uncovering frames an inward disclosure.

luna: The oath holds night as it darkens or withdraws; 81:18 completes the transition with morning breathing, another night-to-dawn pairing. | terra: The oath by the night as it عسعس presents night in transition; beside 81:18 it is the same moving cover and opening morning staged in 89:4 and 89:1.

luna: Morning breathes in تَنَفَّسَ; this joins the section's opening dawn to its final نَفْس through the root ن ف س, while 81:17 supplies the night before it. | terra: The morning that “breathes” (تَنَفَّسَ) directly joins the section’s opening dawn to its closing address to the نَفْس: the rent in darkness is figured as breath.

luna: The sky is split at the opening of the judgment scene; 82:4 later opens the graves, making this a cosmic tearing of the cover beside the section's dawn-rent night and buried earth. | terra: The sky is split open at the Last Day, extending the section's opening rent from the edge of night to the whole celestial cover before seas and graves also open.
terra: The seas are burst open at the cosmic end; the f-j-r root carries rupture from dawn’s life-giving light to an overwhelming eschatological release.

luna: The graves are overturned in بُعْثِرَتْ الْقُبُورُ; the earth's burial-cover is opened, matching the section's cenen/grave sense and its pounded earth. | terra: When the graves are overturned and scattered, the grave-cover named in the section ceases to conceal its occupants.
terra: After sky, sea, and graves open, every soul knows what it sent ahead and left behind; the cosmic rupture culminates in uncovered self-knowledge.
terra: The righteous are in bliss, the immediate bright counterpart to the فُجَّار in 82:14 and therefore to the section’s warning that moral tearing does not release light.

luna: The fujjar end in the Fire; the shared root marks moral rupture as the opposite outcome to the section's opening dawn and its final garden. | terra: The فُجَّار are in blazing fire, showing that the moral rupture sharing dawn’s root opens onto punishment rather than illumination.

luna: The record of the fujjar is in Sijjīn; this directly names the root's moral branch as a destination opposite to the Garden at the section's end. | terra: The record of the فُجَّار is in Sijjīn; the moral tearing named in the section is here fixed into a constricting record and destination.

luna: The wrongdoers' deeds leave rust over their hearts, رَانَ عَلَىٰ قُلُوبِهِمْ; this is a counter-image to the section's moral “tearing” of a cover, showing wrongdoing can also thicken concealment.

luna: The sky splits as the judgment begins; 84:3-4 continue with the earth opened and its contents cast out, a counter-scene joining the section's dawn rupture to its grave-cover image. | terra: The sky splits open at the start of the passage whose earth later spreads and casts out its contents, pairing an opened upper cover with the uncovered grave-earth.
luna: The earth is stretched out before it expels what lies within in 84:4; this gives the section's pounded earth a continuation from flattened ground to opened contents.

luna: The earth casts out what is inside it in أَلْقَتْ مَا فِيهَا, making the hidden contents of the ground visible as the section's grave-cover and crushed-earth images imply. | terra: The earth casts out what is within it and becomes empty, turning the section’s covered grave-earth inside out at the Last Day.
terra: Twilight is sworn by as the visible threshold before the oath turns to night and what it gathers, making the edge between light and cover perceptible.

luna: The oath names night and what it gathers; the exact force of وَمَا وَسَقَ is uncertain, but a gathering night plausibly develops the section's image of darkness drawing a cover over what lies beneath. | terra: The night “and what it gathers” portrays darkness as an enclosing container, a close variant of the section’s cover spread over things.
terra: The full moon is the luminous object gathered within the night of 84:17, paralleling the visible star inside Abraham’s covering darkness.
luna: The oath introduces the night-comer, and 86:3 identifies it as a piercing star; together they make a point of light puncture the darkness like the section's first slit in the night-cover.
luna: The star is called piercing, النَّجْمُ الثَّاقِبُ; 86:1 places it in the night, a specific image of light entering darkness at a point.

luna: Day displays it in جَلَّىٰهَا; 91:4 follows with night covering it, completing the same alternating visibility that the section describes. | terra: The oath by day when it displays the sun contributes the disclosure that answers the covering action of the next ayah.

luna: The oath names night as it covers it in يَغْشَىٰهَا, giving a direct counterpart to the section's night spread over everything. | terra: The oath by night when it covers the sun (يَغْشَىٰهَا) turns night into precisely the spread covering from which the section’s dawn must emerge.

luna: The soul is shaped before 91:8 names its fujur and taqwa; this starts the moral choice that the section's inner restraint and tranquil soul bring into view. | terra: The oath by the نفس and the One who proportioned it begins the passage that places فجور and taqwā within the soul, linking the section’s final addressee to its moral rupture.

luna: The same fujur root is placed opposite taqwa in the soul; the moral rupture is the dark counter-side to the section's dawn-splitting image. | terra: The soul is inspired with its فُجُور and its taqwā; this makes the section’s moral “tearing” one side of an explicit inward boundary.

luna: The one who purifies the soul succeeds; 91:8 defines the competing moral qualities, and this outcome parallels the section's call to the tranquil soul. | terra: The success of the one who purifies the soul states what happens when the inward boundary named in 91:8 is kept rather than torn.

luna: The one who buries or corrupts the soul fails, completing 91:8's fujur/taqwa division as a moral counterpart to the section's two kinds of rupture. | terra: The loss of the one who buries or corrupts the soul gives the dark reversal of purification and resonates with the section’s meeting of moral rupture and burial-cover.

luna: Night is sworn by as it envelops in يَغْشَىٰ, the full-cover state against which the section's torn opening of dawn is visible. | terra: وَٱلَّيْلِ إِذَا يَغْشَىٰ is the section’s night-cover in its fullest action, before any rent or withdrawal has opened it.

luna: Day is sworn by as it appears in تَجَلَّىٰ; it completes 92:1's enveloping night with the visible side of the same transition. | terra: The day “when it unveils itself” (تَجَلَّىٰ) is the answering motion to 92:1’s covering night and closely matches the section’s uncovering as night goes.

luna: The oath by forenoon gives the bright side of the pairing; 93:2 presents night in stillness, so this ayah contributes the daylight counter-scene. | terra: The bright forenoon supplies the opened, illuminated pole of an oath-pair whose other pole is the still night in 93:2.

luna: This oath gives night in its stillness, while the section's night is pictured moving on; it preserves a distinct night-state beside the traveling cover. | terra: The night “when it grows still” is a specific counter-image to 89:4’s night in motion; the same night can be perceived as settled cover or departing traveller.

luna: The night of decree lasts until مَطْلَعِ الْفَجْرِ, making dawn the precise edge where the covered night ends. | terra: The Night of Decree remains peace حَتَّىٰ مَطْلَعِ ٱلْفَجْرِ, so dawn is the exact boundary at which a whole night-state ends.

luna: The verse joins gardens of Eden with God being pleased with the people and their being pleased with Him, closely paralleling the section's soul that is pleased and pleasing as it enters the Garden.
luna: The earth is shaken violently, then 99:2 says it casts out its burdens; this completes the section's pounded-earth and grave-cover image as a single event.

luna: The earth brings out its burdens in أَخْرَجَتِ الْأَرْضُ أَثْقَالَهَا, a direct scene of what was covered below being exposed. | terra: The earth brings out its burdens, another direct uncovering of what burial had hidden beneath the ground.

luna: What is in the graves is scattered in بُعْثِرَ مَا فِي الْقُبُورِ; 100:10 then names what is within the chests, extending judgment's disclosure beyond the earth-cover. | terra: What is in the graves is scattered out, a forceful uncovering of the section’s grave sense of the covering root.
luna: What is in the chests is brought out; 100:9 names the opened graves, and this verse extends the disclosure from earth's cover to hidden inward contents.

luna: The root ف ل ق is explicitly linked by the section to dawn's splitting, but al-falaq can also mean creation generally; on the dawn reading, the refuge begins by naming the Lord of the opening. | terra: Seeking refuge in رَبِّ ٱلْفَلَقِ invokes the same opening by splitting that the section hears in God’s cleaving of morning, while keeping فلق distinct from فجر.
luna: The refuge prayer names darkness when it settles; 113:1's al-falaq supplies the possible dawn-opening counterpart to the section's night and dawn.
